D.t: Dan Ahlers trails by 15.0 and wins 3% of simulations. Closing it takes about 28,890 voters switching sides, or 57,781 more net votes from new turnout.
In 8 of 10 simulations the result lands between R +24.1 and R +5.4. Only an unusual polling error changes the winner.

The polls page average is R +18.0. Your best recent poll is Concord Public Opinion Partners (D) at R +12.7; your worst is Mason-Dixon for South Dakota News Watch and USD Chiesman Center at R +19.2. 3 polls in the last 30 days.

The biggest vote banks for Democrats: Minnehaha, a projected net 4,856 votes; Oglala Lakota, a projected net 2,541 votes; Todd, a projected net 1,505 votes. Every point of extra turnout here is worth more than persuasion anywhere else.
The large counties within 12 points: Minnehaha, D +5.8, 21.7% of the vote; Brown, R +9.4, 4.0% of the vote; Brookings, R +5.0, 3.6% of the vote; Yankton, R +11.9, 2.6% of the vote.

D.h: Where you run behind the 2024 map
D.t: Against the 2024 presidential vote, Dan Ahlers runs furthest behind in Hughes, Lawrence, Butte. That is where the forecast sees voters who backed your side two years ago and have not come back yet.

Groups big enough to move the race: White voters, 91% of voters, 40 to 58, where a 5 point gain is worth 4.57 points; Voters who cast ballots in 2022 and 2024, 74% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.71 points; Voters without a degree, 64% of voters, 41 to 57, where a 5 point gain is worth 3.19 points.

The forecast's worst groups for Dan Ahlers: Immigration voters 16 to 82, Incomes $125K and up 33 to 65, Voters who can afford daily costs 37 to 61. Cutting the loss here is often cheaper than winning new groups.
Registered Democrats cast 30% of the 61,052 ballots in South Dakota so far, against 53% for the other party. That is 4.7 points worse for Democrats than the forecast expected by now.

D.h: What the ballots so far say
D.t: The early vote has moved this forecast 1.6 points away from Dan Ahlers. Election Day has to make it up: the remaining vote must break harder your way than the forecast expects.
